text: On 24 May 2023 the user asked the assistant for popular cooking blogs or websites focused on recipe techniques, and the assistant recommended The Kitchn with its Cooking School section, Serious Eats, America's Test Kitchen, Cook's Illustrated, Food52, NYT Cooking, Epicurious, Bon Appétit and Taste of Science.

The assistant described ChefSteps as a cooking website founded by Grant Achatz that offers in-depth guides on advanced techniques such as sous vide and molecular gastronomy, and described Taste of Science as a site exploring the science behind cooking.

The user had already joined a few online cooking communities as of 24 May 2023, and through them the user engaged in discussions about recipe techniques and shared thoughts on food-related posts, wanting to learn from other food enthusiasts.

The assistant recommended Reddit communities r/Cooking, r/Recipes, r/Food and r/CookingTechniques, food forums Chowhound, Food.com and CookingForums.com, and social media groups such as the Facebook groups Home Cooking Enthusiasts and Cooking Techniques and Recipes, plus Instagram hashtags like #cookingcommunity and #homecooking.

The assistant suggested specialised cooking communities including Stack Exchange's Seasoned Advice Q&A site, The Cooking Subreddit's Discord Server, Food Bloggers Central and The Food Blogger's Forum for food bloggers.

On 24 May 2023 the user asked how to contribute positively to online food discussions without seeming like a know-it-all or a newbie, and the assistant gave twelve tips, including being respectful and humble, reading the whole thread before posting, using I statements, and lurking before leaping.

The assistant advised staying on topic, sharing experiences and techniques rather than only recipes, being open to feedback, proofreading posts before submitting, being mindful of cultural and dietary differences, and following each community's rules and moderator expectations.

The assistant told the user that asking 'dumb' questions is normal, that online cooking communities are generally supportive and encouraging, and that posts may take time to receive responses, so consistent posting and commenting helps build a network.

On 24 May 2023 the user asked for popular cooking YouTube channels or food vloggers focused on recipe techniques and cooking fundamentals, and the assistant named experienced chefs Binging with Babish, Gordon Ramsay, Thomas Keller, Jacques Pépin and Mark Wiens.

The assistant recommended home cook and food vlogger YouTube channels Tasty, Salt Bae, Laura in the Kitchen, The Pioneer Woman and Sorted Food, the UK-based channel aimed at beginners, and specialised channels The King of Random, Food Ranger, It's Alive! with Brad Leone, The Cooking Geek and America's Test Kitchen.

On 24 May 2023 the user asked for cooking YouTube channels focused on specific cuisines, and the assistant suggested Italian channels Laura in the Kitchen, Italian Food Forever and The Pasta Queen, and Chinese channels Chinese Cooking Demystified, The Woks of Life and Chinese Food Made Easy.

The assistant suggested Indian cooking YouTube channels Manjula's Kitchen, Show Me the Curry and Bhavna's Kitchen, and channels for other cuisines: Maangchi for Korean cooking, Cooking with Dog for Japanese cooking, Mexican Please for Mexican cooking and Thai Street Food for Thai cooking.

On 26 May 2023 the user asked the assistant for help creating a system to track the pieces in the user's jewelry collection, and the assistant proposed a spreadsheet with ID, Type, Description, Metal, Gemstones, Acquisition Date, Purchase Price, Current Value, Storage Location and Image columns.

The assistant suggested optional jewelry spreadsheet columns for Designer or Brand, Occasion, Style Era, Condition, Maintenance and Notes, and alternatives to a spreadsheet including the JewelBox or Jewelry Tracker apps, a physical journal or binder, and Evernote or OneNote.

On 26 May 2023 the user wanted to record the sentimental story behind each jewelry piece, including who gave it and when, so the assistant proposed a separate Provenance/Story column covering the giver, the occasion, emotional memories and milestones when the piece was worn.

The user planned to start with the most sentimental pieces, beginning with a silver necklace given to the user by the user's grandma on the user's 18th birthday, which the user lost about two months before 26 May 2023 at a friend's house during a sleepover.

The user still hoped to find the lost silver necklace and planned to ask the user's friend whether the friend had seen it, and planned to note the loss in the Provenance/Story column of the spreadsheet.

The assistant advised adding a History of Ownership or Notable Events column to record losses and repairs, so that the Provenance/Story column for the silver necklace could carry a later update if the necklace was found.

The user planned to record pearl earrings given to the user by the user's parents when the user graduated from high school, associated with good luck, important milestones and confidence, and worn on the day of a stats final about three weeks before 26 May 2023, around 5 May 2023.

The user planned to add a gold chain with a tiny diamond cross pendant borrowed from the user's mom, and needed to ask the mom whether she had seen the small silver clasp the user used to fix the chain when it broke.

The assistant suggested a spreadsheet entry for the gold chain with diamond cross pendant listing Type Necklace, Metal Gold, Gemstones Diamond, storage in the user's possession as a borrowed item, and a Provenance/Story covering how the mom acquired it and why it was borrowed.

On 23 May 2023 the user said the user went grocery shopping at Walmart last Saturday, 20 May 2023, described as exactly a week before, spending around $120, which was higher than expected, but getting 10% off dairy products with a coupon.

On 23 May 2023 the user said the user is open to trying different cuisines but usually makes simple American-style meals like pasta, chicken and veggies, has no food allergies, wants to reduce meat consumption, and plans to prep meals for 5-6 days with leftovers for lunch.

The assistant proposed a veggie-focused meal plan for the coming week: Monday veggie quesadillas, Tuesday spaghetti squash with tomato sauce, Wednesday black bean and sweet potato enchiladas, Thursday roasted veggie wrap, Friday lentil soup and Saturday grilled veggie and cheese sandwich.

The assistant's meal plan included leftover ideas: a veggie omelette for lunch, a veggie lunch wrap with hummus, a sweet potato and black bean soup, a tofu and brown rice stir-fry for dinner, a lentil salad with vinaigrette, and a veggie omelette for brunch.

The user said the user especially liked the veggie quesadillas and lentil soup, and wanted a simple chicken stir-fry using chicken breast the user bought last week at Walmart, the week of 15 May 2023.

The assistant's Chicken and Veggie Stir-Fry used 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, 2 cups mixed veggies, 2 cloves garlic, 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 teaspoon soy sauce, salt and pepper, served over brown rice or whole-grain noodles, and took about 20-25 minutes in total.

On 23 May 2023 the user asked for a recipe combining chicken breast and ground beef, and the assistant suggested Chicken and Beef Tacos using 1 lb ground beef, 1/2 lb finely chopped chicken breast, one diced onion, two cloves garlic, a packet of taco seasoning, bell peppers and tomatoes.

The assistant suggested an alternative of Chicken and Beef Meatballs, made by combining the cooked chicken and beef mixture with breadcrumbs, egg and seasonings, then baking or frying and serving with marinara sauce and pasta.

On 23 May 2023 the user said the user would try the Chicken and Beef Tacos recipe during the coming week, liking the idea of combining ground beef and chicken breast and planning to customise the tacos with favourite toppings.

On 23 May 2023 the user asked for tips on organising the pantry and fridge to reduce food waste and make meal planning easier, and the assistant advised purging expired items, grouping similar goods, using labelled airtight containers and zoning the fridge.

The assistant advised keeping raw meat and fish covered at the bottom of the fridge, labelling and dating leftovers, keeping a use-up list, and planning meals around existing stock before shopping, while storing heavy canned goods on lower shelves.

On 21 May 2023 the user said the user and the user's sister went to Trader Joe's the week of 1 May 2023 and spent around $80 between them on pre-packaged meals and snacks, which the assistant described as a great deal.

The assistant suggested chicken breast recipes Lemon Garlic Chicken, Chicken Fajitas, Chicken Parmesan and Chicken Caesar Wraps, and ground beef recipes Spaghetti Bolognese, Tacos, Meatball Subs and Shepherd's Pie.

On 21 May 2023 the user said the user would try Chicken Fajitas and Spaghetti Bolognese that week and asked for a grocery list, noting that the chicken breast and ground beef were already bought last week at Walmart, the week of 8 May 2023.

The assistant's grocery list for Chicken Fajitas and Spaghetti Bolognese included bell peppers, onions, tortillas, sour cream, salsa, spaghetti, canned crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, Parmesan, fajita seasoning, Italian seasoning and olive oil, with optional cilantro, basil and shredded cheese.

On 21 May 2023 the user asked for cauliflower gnocchi recipes, having bought several packs at Trader Joe's with the user's sister, and the assistant suggested seven dishes: tomato sauce, brown butter sage, pesto cream, roasted vegetable bowl, meat sauce, garlic shrimp and mushroom cream.

The assistant's cauliflower gnocchi tips were to follow the package instructions for cooking time, handle the gnocchi gently, avoid overcooking so they do not turn mushy, and pair them with lighter sauces because they absorb flavours easily.

On 21 May 2023 the user asked for storage tips for reusable containers and bags, which the user had been using more since buying more items in bulk, and the assistant advised a designated container station, stacking and nesting containers, and labelling containers by contents.

The assistant advised folding reusable bags into a drawer or basket, using a bag holder or clip, sorting bags by type, keeping bags visible near the entrance, and cleaning and drying containers and bags before storing them out of direct sunlight.

On 21 May 2023 the user said the user had been reducing household waste by buying nuts, granola and dried fruits in bulk, which helped the user avoid single-use plastics and save money in the long run.

The assistant said bulk buying reduces packaging waste, saves money through lower unit prices, cuts store trips and encourages mindful consumption, and suggested glass jars or cloth bags, planning shopping lists and a first in, first out rule.

On 21 May 2023 the user said the user placed an online order with Thrive Market in April 2023, getting good deals on organic and sustainable products, and was considering ordering from Thrive Market again soon.

The assistant described Thrive Market as offering a wide selection of bulk nuts, seeds, grains and snacks, plus household and personal care products, with eco-friendly packaging and environmentally responsible suppliers, and suggested comparing Amazon Bulk and BulkApothecary.

The assistant suggested checking local co-ops or natural food stores for bulk options and asked the user about the user's experience with Thrive Market's customer service and shipping, and which products the user enjoyed.

On 25 May 2023 the user said the user planned meals using chicken breast and ground beef bought last week, the week of 15 May 2023, and said the user placed a Thrive Market online order in April 2023 spending around $150 on organic and sustainable products.

The assistant's recipes using chicken breast included Lemon Garlic Chicken, Chicken Fajitas, Chicken Caesar Salad, Chicken Tikka Masala and Chicken and Veggie Kabobs, and its ground beef recipes included Spaghetti Bolognese, Tacos, Meatball Subs, Shepherd's Pie and Stuffed Bell Peppers.

On 25 May 2023 the user said the user especially wanted to try Chicken Fajitas and Spaghetti Bolognese, and planned to order reusable containers and bags from Thrive Market to reduce household waste even further.

The assistant recommended glass containers with airtight lids, stainless steel containers, collapsible silicone containers, cotton or jute produce bags, reusable grocery bags, insulated bags, snack bags, beeswax wraps, reusable water bottles and silicone baking mats.

The assistant advised choosing reusable containers and bags made from recycled plastic, stainless steel, cotton, jute or other natural fibres, and considering durability and ease of cleaning when shopping on Thrive Market.
On 25 May 2023 the user said the user had been using reusable containers from the user's last Thrive Market online order to reduce household waste, and planned to start meal prepping.

The assistant advised cooling meals to room temperature within 2 hours, refrigerating them within 30 minutes of cooking, using airtight leak-proof containers, labelling and dating each container, and eating refrigerated meals within 3-5 days.
The assistant said meal preps can be frozen in airtight containers or freezer bags for up to 3-4 months and should be reheated to an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) to ensure food safety.

On 25 May 2023 the user asked for a grocery list based on the recipes discussed, and the assistant listed produce such as bell peppers, onions, mushrooms, cherry tomatoes, broccoli, lettuce, spinach, lemons, avocados and cilantro, plus 4-5 lbs boneless skinless chicken breast and 1-2 lbs ground beef.

The assistant's grocery list also included pantry items such as whole wheat pasta, quinoa, olive oil, coconut oil, fajita and taco seasoning, tomato sauce, canned diced tomatoes, balsamic vinegar and soy sauce, plus Greek yogurt, eggs, tortillas, salsa and hummus.

The assistant listed beverages, snacks, baking supplies, pantry items and personal care items as categories that often have high Ibotta cashback rates.

On 25 May 2023 the user said the user planned to buy organic produce, meat, dairy, quinoa and olive oil at Publix, and repeated that the user placed a Thrive Market online order the previous month, in April 2023, spending around $150.

The assistant said buying organic produce, meat and dairy reduces environmental impact and exposure to pesticides, that quinoa and olive oil are sustainable pantry choices, and that the user should check Publix's organic options for deals.

On 26 May 2023 the user said the user is open to any cuisine, wants to cook more meals at home to reduce food waste, and plans five dinners plus a few lunch ideas, with staples including rice, pasta and canned goods from the user's last Walmart trip.

The assistant proposed five dinners: Monday Creamy Tomato Pasta Bake, Tuesday Chicken Fajita Stir-Fry, Wednesday Lentil Soup, Thursday Balsamic Glazed Chicken and Roasted Vegetables, and Friday Black Bean and Sweet Potato Enchiladas, each designed to use up leftovers.

The assistant suggested lunch ideas made from dinner leftovers, or a simple salad of mixed greens, canned beans and a vinaigrette dressing.

On 26 May 2023 the user asked for a grocery list organised by aisle or category, and the assistant listed produce, meat and seafood, dairy and eggs, canned goods, pantry, bakery and miscellaneous items, such as 1 lb ground beef, 1-2 lbs chicken breast, 1 cup heavy cream and one loaf of crusty bread.

The assistant estimated the total cost of the 26 May 2023 grocery list at $74-$115 using average prices, excluding the $10 delivery fee, with produce around $25-$35, meat and seafood $9-$17, and dairy and eggs $9-$15.

On 26 May 2023 the user said the user aimed to stay around $80-$90 for the groceries, including the delivery fee, and asked whether ingredients such as canned tomatoes could be substituted to reduce cost.

The assistant suggested cost-saving substitutions: canned tomatoes for fresh, frozen vegetables, ground turkey or chicken instead of beef, shredded cheese instead of mozzarella, and omitting balsamic glaze, estimating a reduced total of about $60-$75.

The assistant suggested using pantry staples already at home, such as dried oregano, basil or cumin, canned beans or tomatoes, coconut oil or apple cider vinegar, rice, quinoa, pasta, soy sauce, hot sauce or broth, after checking their expiry dates.

On 11 August 2023 the user said the user felt overwhelmed by work tasks and asked the assistant to prioritise them by urgency and importance, and the assistant proposed the Eisenhower Matrix with its four quadrants.

The user's four work tasks as of 11 August 2023 were: finish the project report due the end of the week of 7 August 2023, respond to a client email about the project timeline due 11 August 2023, prepare for the team meeting due 12 August 2023, and review and update the project plan due the week of 14 August 2023.

The assistant ranked responding to the client email as urgent and important, to be done first, and placed finishing the project report and reviewing the project plan in the important but not urgent category to be scheduled.

The assistant said preparing for the team meeting is important but can be done alongside the project report or during breaks, such as a lunch break or just before the meeting, and advised focusing on one task at a time.
On 11 August 2023 the user said the user has been practising yoga twice a week, which has been helping the user relax and focus, and asked for stress-reducing apps or meditation techniques.

The assistant recommended the stress-reducing apps Headspace, Calm, Insight Timer and Breethe, and the meditation techniques mindfulness meditation, loving-kindness meditation, body scan and 4-7-8 breathing.

The assistant advised starting meditation with 5-10 minute sessions, building it into a daily routine such as right after waking or before bed, choosing a quiet space, and being patient when the mind wanders.
On 11 August 2023 the user said the user uses meditation to set intentions and focus on goals for the day.

The assistant's mindfulness advice for busy days included eating and walking mindfully, one-minute breathing exercises, short breaks, using the Headspace, Calm or Insight Timer apps, and practising mindfulness during transit or while waiting in line.

The assistant said mindfulness can be fitted into a busy day by setting phone reminders, choosing a fixed time such as first thing in the morning or before bed, and treating mindfulness as a form of self-care.
